claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. POL-RD-01 fixes the governing distance as gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 4.05 km, against a booked optimal of 3.20 km — an excess of 0.85 km, or 26.56% of optimal. Both limbs of the establishment test pass: 0.85 km exceeds 20% of optimal (0.64 km) and exceeds the 0.80 km absolute threshold. The trip_record convenience copy of 4.00 km would yield exactly 0.80 km and fail the strict 'greater than' test; POL-RD-01 expressly makes the trace figure govern and forbids citing the rounded copy for the threshold test, so the trace figure is the one that decides this case.

No clause excuses the excess as an external traffic event. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching it, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. There is no such advisory: the bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02822-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0, and the trace's own advisory_area block carries an empty advisories list. The driver's statement 'Followed the app' asserts no traffic cause and names no artifact. Under POL-RD-13 the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight.

The rider requested no detour, so POL-RD-04 cannot exculpate the driver. That clause requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped within the window it sets and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of the waypoint named by chat_message.waypoint_hint. The chat log for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate; POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record.

The endpoints were never amended, so the booked optimal stands. POL-RD-05 re-runs the threshold against an amended optimal only where an endpoint was moved after booking. On the trip record both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote is triggered and the baseline remains 3.20 km.

This is a metered trip, not an upfront-quoted one, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route. POL-RD-11 applies only where fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null. Here fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-02 runs in full against the booked optimal route.

This was not a pooled trip. POL-RD-12 displaces the POL-RD-01 baseline only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL. The trip record shows RYDE_X and carries no solo_optimal_distance_km, so the single-rider optimal of 3.20 km is the correct baseline and no co-rider distance is in issue.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 3.20 optimal km + 0.28 x 6.0 optimal min) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 waiting_time_fee - 0.00 promo_discount = 8.68. Charged_total is 9.28, so the refund is 9.28 - 8.68 = 0.60, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which leaves it at 0.60.

The refund is neither de minimis nor full, so the correct outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the 0.60. At 0.60 it is at or above the SGD 0.50 de_minimis_refund floor, so NO_ACTION does not apply, and it is 6.47% of charged_total, far below the 90% full_refund_share, so no FULL_REFUND arises.

No pass-through line is added on top of, or double-counted against, that figure. POL-RD-09(1) comprehends off-route ERP inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and here the fare carries 0.00 of ERP and tolls and 0.00 airport surcharge, so the 0.60 already is the whole of the rider's recovery and nothing further is owed on the pass-through lines.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and needs no corroboration. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap exceeding 90 seconds, a straight-line jump exceeding 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace carries zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, a 10-second sample interval and 100% coverage across 37 fixes, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met and no independent source under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and the driver has not shifted it back. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02822, and the trip_start timestamp on the record (12:34:20) matches the trace's first fix (12:34:20), so the artifacts describe the same trip; the excess of 0.85 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden then lies on the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause, and 'Followed the app' names neither, so it is discarded and carries no weight. The rider's own citable counters add no corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, well below the 4 that POL-RD-08 would require.

The driver's profile supplies no ground to resist the refund, and no uplift is available on it either. On the only counters POL-RD-06 makes citable for its test, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below the 3 required) and 1/402 = 0.0025 (below the 0.05 ratio), with completed_trips_90d of 402, so no pattern is established; and because the excess of 0.85 km is below both materiality limbs (50% of optimal = 1.60 km, and 8.0 km absolute), no materiality arises and no POL-RD-06(c) referral follows. The rider's entitlement is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial figure of 0.60, undiminished, and every other field on either profile is context only under POL-GEN-01.

claims.text: The distance test is measured on the trace and only the trace: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.05 km against the booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.85 km or 26.56%, and POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km (4.0 km, a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement) for the threshold test. That 0.85 km is the whole of what the rider's evidence proves on distance; nothing in the bundle shows a larger excess, whatever the claim text implies.

The remedy for a proven excess on a metered fare is arithmetic, not the fare itself. Reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0) and the platform fee from the fare breakdown: charged_total is 9.28; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 8.68; refund = 9.28 - 8.68 = 0.60, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 0.60. The rider's claim to the whole $9.28 fare is more than fifteen times what POL-RD-02 yields, and 0.60 is only 6.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would make it a full refund.

The deviation is not material. POL-RD-01 sets the material gates at an excess greater than 50% of optimal_distance_km or greater than 8.0 km in absolute terms, and the proven excess is 26.56% and 0.85 km. Neither gate is met, so the POL-RD-06 uplift to a FULL_REFUND of charged_total under limb (b) is unavailable and no conduct referral under limb (c) arises.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted under POL-RD-06, no pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the three-flag floor, and 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 402 is a ratio of 0.0025, below the 0.05 threshold, with the 40-trip minimum satisfied. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure that POL-RD-06 names (POL-GEN-01). No balance can be resolved against the driver on profile evidence and no referral under limb (c) follows.

No separate pass-through or billing-integrity correction is due. The fare breakdown carries no ERP line at all - the on-optimal and off-optimal ERP totals are both 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty - it carries no airport surcharge, and the waiting-time fee is 0.00, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct and no standalone POL-RD-09(4) refund, finding or referral arises. The only money that moves on this trip is the distance-and-time recomputation under POL-RD-02.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 37 fixes at a 10-second sample interval spanning 100% of the trip, with no gaps and a maximum gap between consecutive fixes of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met. The excess therefore stands at the measured trace figure on a fully usable record, no independent-corroboration question is raised, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged: this case is decidable on this trip's own evidence and should be closed on the arithmetic rather than held.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver.

This was a metered RYDE_X trip (TRP-02822) from Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 to Blk 456 Hougang Ave 10 on 13 September 2026, charged at SGD 9.28.

ROUTE DEVIATION — ESTABLISHED, AND ON THE TRACE. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern, and it is 4.05 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km (4.00 km) is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 3.20 km the excess is 0.85 km, or 26.56% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 0.85 km is greater than 0.80 km absolute and greater than 20% of optimal (0.64 km). On the rounded 4.00 km copy the excess would be exactly 0.80 km and would have failed the strict 'greater than' test, so which artifact governs decides this case and the trace governs. The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes: 37 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) was required, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC. fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route and POL-RD-02 runs. On separate lines: charged_total 9.28; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 3.20 optimal km [2.40] + 0.28 x 6.0 optimal min [1.68]) x the surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo discount = 8.68; refund = 9.28 - 8.68 = 0.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so NO_ACTION does not apply, and at 6.47% of charged_total it is far below the 90% that would make it a full refund. The rider's claim to the whole SGD 9.28 is not supported; the arithmetic yields 0.60, not 9.28, and the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 0.60.

NO EXCUSING CLAUSE APPLIES. No endpoint was amended after booking (POL-RD-05: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so the booked optimal of 3.20 km stands. No rider-requested detour can be shown: the chat log carries zero messages, so there is no instruction and no waypoint_hint (POL-RD-04). The trip was not pooled (POL-RD-12: vehicle_type RYDE_X, solo_optimal_distance_km null). No traffic cause exonerates the excess: there is no advisory on file (POL-RD-03 is unavailable, POL-RD-13), and the driver's statement 'Followed the app' names neither an artifact nor a clause, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The missing advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02822-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no party cited it as the ground of an exculpatory excuse, so it is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) trigger.

BILLING LINES AND COMPENSATION. The fare carries no ERP, no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting fee (all 0.00), so POL-RD-09 corrects nothing and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding or referral arises; POL-RD-09(1) simply confirms nothing is added on top of the 0.60. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (4.0 km) falls only 0.05 km short of the trace distance, far below the 1.0 km shortfall POL-RD-04 requires.

PROFILE EVIDENCE. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 402 is 0.0025 (below 0.05), so the POL-RD-06 uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral do not arise; in any event the excess of 0.85 km is below both materiality gates. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration was required. Every other field on either profile — including the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags — is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used as a ground.

DISCARDED CLAIM. The rider's submission that no traffic clause excuses the excess cited the impaired advisory EV-ADVIS-02822-01 without disclosing its impairment (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). It was discarded on that ground by the mechanical check, and the conclusion it drew — that no advisory is on file — is reached here from the absent artifact itself, not from that claim.

NO REFERRAL FIRES: no POL-RD-06(c) conduct review, no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral and no POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record. The monetary effect, SGD 0.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. This ruling is provisional and either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
